data-protection-baseline.title: Compliance Manager assessments - Microsoft Purview
data-protection-baseline.notes: The Data Protection Baseline is the default assessment that Microsoft supplies in Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager so a tenant has a starting point from day one. It bundles a set of controls for key regulations and standards covering data protection and general data governance, drawn mainly from NIST CSF, ISO, FedRAMP and the GDPR. It is included at every subscription level, so it does not depend on a premium license, unlike the premium AI regulation templates that consume purchased premium licenses. The first time an admin opens Compliance Manager, the baseline is used to calculate an initial compliance score, based on signals collected from the organization's Microsoft 365 solutions. It shows how the organization measures up against those standards and suggests improvement actions. It is distinct from the separate baseline assessment for Microsoft 365 Copilot, which is derived from global AI regulations. Compliance Manager becomes more valuable as teams add assessments for their own regulatory needs, and at least one assessment must always exist for the tool to work.

data-protection-impact-assessment.title: Art. 35 GDPR - Data protection impact assessment
data-protection-impact-assessment.notes: Article 35 of the GDPR requires the controller to carry out a data protection impact assessment before processing begins whenever a type of processing, especially one using new technologies, is likely to result in a high risk to people's rights and freedoms. One assessment can cover a set of similar processing operations with similar risks. The article names three cases where it is expressly required: systematic and extensive evaluation of personal aspects through automated processing or profiling that leads to significant decisions, large-scale processing of special categories of data or criminal conviction data, and large-scale systematic monitoring of publicly accessible areas. Supervisory authorities publish lists of operations that do and do not need one. The assessment must contain at least four elements: a systematic description of the processing and its purposes, an assessment of necessity and proportionality, an assessment of the risks to data subjects, and the measures planned to address those risks, including safeguards and security measures. The controller must seek the advice of the data protection officer if one is designated, should seek the views of data subjects where appropriate, and must review the assessment when the risk changes.

data-transfer-object.title: Data transfer object - Wikipedia
data-transfer-object.notes: A data transfer object is a simple object that carries data between processes. Apart from storing, retrieving, serializing and deserializing its own data, it has no behavior and should hold no business logic; in some languages it is expressed as a record or struct. The pattern is credited to Martin Fowler's Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture. Its purpose is to cut the cost of remote calls such as web services, where most of the expense is round-trip time between client and server: data that would need several calls is aggregated into one object and sent in a single call, with serialization support so it can travel over the wire. In model-view-viewmodel architectures a DTO may be called the viewmodel. The article distinguishes DTOs from business objects, which contain logic, from data access objects, which handle persistence, and from value objects, which are a different concept that Java sources sometimes conflated with DTOs. It also notes a frequent misuse: applying DTOs inside a single process where no remote call exists, which Fowler has criticized because the benefit then disappears.

database-normalization.title: Database normalization - Wikipedia
database-normalization.notes: Database normalization is the process of structuring a relational database according to a series of normal forms in order to reduce data redundancy and improve data integrity. It was proposed by Edgar F. Codd as part of the relational model, with later contributions from Boyce, Fagin and Date. Normalization can be done by synthesis, when designing a new database, or by decomposition, when improving an existing one. It targets three kinds of anomalies: insertion anomalies, where a fact cannot be stored without unrelated data; update anomalies, where the same fact stored in several rows becomes inconsistent; and deletion anomalies, where removing one fact unintentionally removes another. The normal forms build on each other: first normal form (1970) requires single-valued fields, second and third normal form (1971) remove partial and transitive dependencies on keys, Boyce-Codd normal form (1974) tightens the rule on functional dependencies, and fourth and fifth normal form deal with multivalued and join dependencies. A relation is informally called normalized once it reaches third normal form. Forms beyond fourth are mainly academic, and sixth normal form is unsuited to transaction-heavy systems.

dataverse-elastic-tables.title: Elastic tables - Dataverse developer documentation
dataverse-elastic-tables.notes: Elastic tables are a Dataverse table type backed by Azure Cosmos DB that scale horizontally for large data volumes, high throughput and unpredictable or fast-growing workloads. Rows are split into logical partitions according to the system column partitionid. Once a row is created its partition id cannot be changed, values must stay under 1,024 bytes, and each logical partition can hold 20 GB, so a high-cardinality value is recommended; if none is given, Dataverse falls back to the primary key. A time-to-live column lets rows delete themselves after a set number of seconds. Consistency is strong only within a logical session, using a session token to read your own writes. Unlike standard tables, elastic tables do not support multi-record transactions: batches and changesets are not atomic, plug-in errors do not roll back the data operation, and deep inserts fail. They suit semi-structured or changing data, high read and write volumes and expiring data, while standard tables remain better for relational modeling, complex joins and strict transactional consistency. The page lists known issues, such as rows removed by TTL staying in data lakes synced through Synapse Link.

dataverse-hierarchy-security.title: Hierarchy security - Power Platform admin
dataverse-hierarchy-security.notes: Hierarchy security is an extension of the Dataverse security model that sits on top of business units, security roles, sharing and teams. It is disabled by default and gives more granular record access than business units alone, at lower maintenance cost. Two models exist. The manager hierarchy follows the Manager lookup on the user record, so managers reach their reports' data; by default a manager must be in the same or a parent business unit. The position hierarchy uses admin-defined job positions in a tree with users tagged to positions, works across business units and suits cases where managers need to see work in other units. Direct reports or lower positions give the manager Read, Write, Append and AppendTo, while non-direct levels are read-only. A configurable depth limits how many levels down the read-only access reaches. The manager still needs at least user-level Read on the table, and hierarchy access is additive to what roles already grant. Microsoft advises keeping the effective hierarchy under any manager to 50 users or fewer and avoiding many business units. Enabling is done per environment in the Power Platform admin center, with a choice of which tables take part.

dataverse-indexing.title: Query anti-patterns - Dataverse developer documentation
dataverse-indexing.notes: This page does not give a full explanation of Dataverse indexing, but it states how database indexes affect query performance in Dataverse. Dataverse cannot use database indexes when a query filters with a leading wildcard, which forces SQL to scan the whole table, and such table scans can occur even if other conditions in the same query use trailing wildcards. Because of database collation rules, search strings beginning with a hyphen or apostrophe can behave like leading wildcards unless a non-wildcard character comes before the percent sign; for example a pattern such as a hyphen followed by digits and a trailing wildcard can use an index, while a hyphen followed immediately by a wildcard cannot. Memo columns and string columns with a maximum length above 850 count as large text columns, which are too large to index effectively, so using them in filter conditions performs badly. The guidance is to filter on string columns shorter than 850 and to use Dataverse search for large text. The page does not cover creating custom indexes or alternate keys.

dataverse-record-sharing.title: Sharing and assigning records - Dataverse developer documentation
dataverse-record-sharing.notes: Sharing lets a user give other users or teams access to a specific Dataverse record, which is useful for people whose security roles have only Basic access. A salesperson who can see only their own opportunities, for instance, can share one with a colleague so both can track it. Three SDK messages manage shares: GrantAccess shares a record with a user, team or organization, ModifyAccess changes the rights of an existing share, and RevokeAccess removes it. Each share carries an access-rights mask, such as Read, Write, Assign or Share, and rights can differ per principal. Access is cumulative, so someone with a direct share and a team share gets the union of both. A share can never exceed the table privileges in the user's role: without Read on accounts, a shared account stays invisible. Children of a shared parent can inherit the share through cascade behavior, and inherited sharing is tracked separately from direct sharing. The page recommends sharing only necessary records with the smallest practical set of users. It does not describe the internal principal object access table.

dataverse-table-relationships.title: Create and edit table relationships - Power Apps
dataverse-table-relationships.notes: Dataverse has two true relationship types: one-to-many and many-to-many. The many-to-one view is just the child-side perspective of a one-to-many relationship. A one-to-many relationship is implemented with a lookup column on the related table, and adding a lookup column creates such a relationship; a many-to-many relationship uses a hidden intersect table. Table relationships are formal metadata used for efficient queries and reporting, whereas connections are informal links such as friends with or formerly worked for. Relationship behavior controls how actions on a parent row cascade to child rows for assign, reparent, share, unshare, delete and merge. Options include Cascade All, Cascade Active, Cascade User Owned, Cascade None, Remove Link and Restrict, which blocks deleting a parent that has children. A relationship is parental when at least one action cascades; usually only one parental relationship exists per table pair, and a custom table cannot be the primary side of a cascading relationship with a system table. Lookups return the related row's primary name to anyone who can see the lookup, so sensitive data should not live in primary name columns.

dataverse-teams.title: Manage teams - Power Platform admin
dataverse-teams.notes: Dataverse has three team types. Owner teams can own records and have security roles assigned, with members added manually. Access teams cannot own records or hold roles; instead, records are shared with the team, which grants Read, Write and Append on those specific records. Microsoft Entra group teams map to Entra security or Microsoft 365 groups, can own records and hold roles like owner teams, and have their membership derived dynamically from the directory group when users access an environment, so the Entra admin manages who belongs. A team belongs to one business unit but can include users from others, and a user can be in several teams. Each business unit has a system-managed owner team. An owner team can be converted to an access team only after its records are reassigned, the conversion removes its role assignments, and converting the business unit's default owner team is irreversible. Adding members to an owner team requires privileges at least equal to the team's roles, and disabled users cannot be added by default. Deleting a team is permanent.

dax-calculate-function.title: CALCULATE function (DAX) - Microsoft Learn
dax-calculate-function.notes: CALCULATE evaluates an expression in a modified filter context and works in measures, calculated columns, calculated tables and visual calculations. Its syntax is an expression followed by optional filter arguments. Filters can be Boolean expressions, table expressions, or filter modifier functions such as REMOVEFILTERS, ALL, ALLEXCEPT, KEEPFILTERS, USERELATIONSHIP and CROSSFILTER. Boolean filters are limited to columns of a single table and cannot reference measures, use a nested CALCULATE or call table-scanning functions. When a filter targets a column not yet filtered, it is added; when the column is already filtered, the new filter overwrites the existing one unless KEEPFILTERS is used. A typical use is a measure that returns revenue only for blue products, or a ratio to total that divides sales by CALCULATE with REMOVEFILTERS on the channel column. Used without filters, CALCULATE also performs context transition by converting the current row context into an equivalent filter context. CALCULATE is not supported in DirectQuery mode when used in calculated columns or row-level security rules.

dax-context-transition.title: CALCULATE function (DAX) - Microsoft Learn (context transition section)
dax-context-transition.notes: Context transition is described in the remarks of the CALCULATE page. When CALCULATE is called, including without any filter arguments, it converts the current row context into an equivalent filter context. This is needed when an expression that summarizes model data, rather than a model measure, must be evaluated inside a row context, such as in a calculated column or within an iterator function. When a model measure is referenced inside a row context, the transition happens automatically. The page's example is a calculated column that classifies customers: CALCULATE sums sales for the current row's customer, because the row's customer key becomes a filter, and ALLEXCEPT removes all other filters on the Customer table so the total reflects that single customer's lifetime sales. Customers below a threshold of 2,500 are labeled Low and the rest High. Context transition is therefore the mechanism that lets row-by-row logic see the related data in the model. The page also notes that CALCULATE in calculated columns is not supported under DirectQuery.

decorator-pattern.title: Decorator pattern - Wikipedia
decorator-pattern.notes: The decorator pattern is one of the 23 Gang of Four design patterns. It wraps an object to add behavior to that one instance without changing other instances of the same class, so responsibilities can be added or removed at run time rather than at compile time through subclassing. A decorator implements the same interface as the object it wraps, keeps a reference to it, forwards calls and performs extra work before or after, overriding only the methods that need new behavior. Decorators can be stacked in any combination, and the client uses the outermost object without knowing it is wrapped. This supports the single responsibility principle by splitting concerns across small classes, and the open-closed principle because behavior is extended without editing existing source. It avoids the explosion of subclasses that would be needed for every combination of features and works for classes that cannot be modified. Common uses are Java and .NET I/O streams and adding UI effects. The article cautions that stacking order can matter and many layers can complicate interfaces. It also stresses that the pattern is distinct from Python's decorator syntax.

delta-lake-compaction.title: Optimizations - Delta Lake documentation
delta-lake-compaction.notes: In Delta Lake, compaction coalesces many small files into fewer larger ones to speed up read queries. It is run with the OPTIMIZE command, in SQL on a path or table name, optionally restricted by a partition predicate, or through the Python and Scala API. The feature is available from Delta Lake 1.2.0, and the programmatic API from 2.0. OPTIMIZE uses bin-packing, which aims for files that are evenly balanced by size on disk rather than by row count, and this operation is idempotent: running it twice on the same data has no effect the second time. Readers use snapshot isolation, so queries are not interrupted while OPTIMIZE removes the old files from the transaction log, it makes no data changes so results before and after are identical, and it does not disturb streams that read the table as a source. The command returns statistics such as minimum, maximum and total sizes of removed and added files. A related option, OPTIMIZE with ZORDER BY, colocates related data for better data skipping on frequently filtered high-cardinality columns, but unlike bin-packing it is not idempotent because each run re-clusters all files in a partition.

desire-paths.title: Desire path - Wikipedia
desire-paths.notes: A desire path is an unplanned trail worn by repeated foot traffic, usually marking the shortest or easiest route through a natural area or greenspace. Transport planners call it a desire line, and informal names include social trail, game trail and cow path. Paths form where official routes are indirect or missing; trampling wears away vegetation and soil, and later walkers follow the visible track, so it becomes entrenched. As few as 15 passages can create a distinct trail. Some desire paths eventually become formal trails or streets, and park managers read them as indicators of where activity concentrates. Barriers such as fences and signs often fail to stop them, so planners may pave them or leave land unpaved first and then build along observed routes. The article notes the term is also used in software design for the workarounds users adopt around a tool's limits, linked to the principle of paving the cowpaths, meaning building official features around existing behavior. It is also used as a metaphor for intuitive design and the wisdom of crowds. Ecologically, paths can fragment habitat and encourage invasive species.

developer-experience.title: Developer experience - Wikipedia
developer-experience.notes: Developer experience, abbreviated DX, is a field of software engineering that studies how developers think, feel and interact with their tools, environments and processes, drawing on human-computer interaction, UX, organizational psychology and software engineering. The term was popularized around 2011 by Jeremiah Lee Cohick, and a first formal academic definition by Fagerholm and Munch followed in 2012, built on cognition, affect and conation. Later frameworks include SPACE from 2021 and the DevEx framework from 2023, which names feedback loops, cognitive load and flow state as core dimensions. Feedback loops cover how quickly systems respond to developer actions such as builds and reviews; cognitive load is the mental effort tasks require; flow is focused, energized work. Platform engineering is described as the practical layer that implements DX through self-service tooling. Measurement mixes perceptual data, such as surveys, with workflow data, such as the DORA metrics of deployment frequency, lead time, recovery time and change failure rate. Critics warn that poorly designed metrics invite gaming and that activity should not be confused with productivity.

device-twin.title: Understand and use device twins in IoT Hub - Azure IoT Hub
device-twin.notes: A device twin is a JSON document that stores state information for a device, including metadata, configuration and conditions. IoT Hub keeps one twin per registered device identity, creating it with the identity and deleting it with it, and the feature is available in the standard tier. The document contains read-only device identity properties, tags, desired properties and reported properties. Tags are readable and writable only by back-end apps and are invisible to the device. Desired properties are written by the back end and observed by the device, which applies them and reports the outcome in reported properties, which the device writes and back-end apps query. Typical uses are storing metadata in the cloud, reporting current state such as connectivity type, synchronizing long-running workflows like firmware updates, and querying fleets. Reported properties suit last known values, while time-series telemetry belongs in device-to-cloud messages. Size limits are 8 KB for tags and 32 KB each for desired and reported properties, with up to 10 levels of nesting. Optimistic concurrency uses an etag and an increasing version number, and devices should re-read the full desired document after reconnecting because notifications are not stored for offline devices.

digital-signal-processor.title: Digital signal processor - Wikipedia
digital-signal-processor.notes: A digital signal processor is a microprocessor whose design is tailored to digital signal processing, typically measuring, filtering or compressing real-world analog signals after they have been digitized. General-purpose processors can run such algorithms but may fail to keep up in real time and use more power, which is a drawback in portable devices. DSP architectures use specialized instruction sets, with dedicated multiply-accumulate instructions, often Harvard or modified von Neumann memory layouts that allow several memory accesses per cycle, hardware loop control, circular-buffer addressing, saturation arithmetic and mostly fixed-point math for low cost, although floating-point DSPs suit applications needing wide dynamic range. Later generations added pipelining and VLIW, SIMD and superscalar designs. Typical applications include audio signal processing, telecommunications, image processing, radar, sonar, speech recognition and consumer electronics such as phones and HDTV. Early milestones include the Texas Instruments chip in the 1978 Speak and Spell toy, often called the first DSP, and the TMS32010 from 1983. The article gives little detail on specific audio algorithms such as echo reduction.

distributed-order-management.title: Distributed order management (DOM) - Dynamics 365 Commerce
distributed-order-management.notes: Distributed order management in Dynamics 365 Commerce is an omnichannel order fulfillment optimization solution. It helps retailers fulfill orders from the best sources in the supply chain network, so products reach customers in the right quantities, from the right places and at the right time, while maximizing profit, minimizing cost and meeting service-level requirements. It addresses conflicting needs in multichannel networks where orders can be filled from many channels and where businesses must react to order changes, supplier problems and demand spikes. DOM uses mixed integer programming and predictive analysis models, optimizing both at batch level and for single orders. Inputs include the distance between fulfillment sources and shipping destinations, cost factors defined as optimization objectives, and rules defined as constraints, such as inventory at fulfillment nodes; an example objective is to minimize cost by fulfilling from the closest sources. Several DOM profiles can be defined, each with a different optimization strategy, so fulfillment can be tailored to a type of business or consumer segment. The overview itself leaves detailed topics such as rules, cost configuration, processing and limitations to linked articles.

distributed-transactions.title: Distributed transaction - Wikipedia
distributed-transactions.notes: A distributed transaction runs across several network nodes, usually because the data lives in different places, and its defining property is atomicity: it completes entirely or not at all. It is not limited to databases, and the X/Open XA model became a de facto standard for how transaction components behave. When a transaction spans multiple databases, it must stay synchronized while still providing ACID properties, and isolation is the hardest. Each database may guarantee serializability on its own, yet global serializability can still be violated; most commercial databases use strong strict two-phase locking, which ensures global serializability only if every participant uses it. Two-phase commit is the common algorithm for completing such transactions correctly and is normally applied to updates that commit within milliseconds to a few minutes. Long-lived distributed transactions, such as booking a flight, a rental car and a hotel together, are unsuited to it because resources would stay locked too long; they instead rely on compensating transactions, optimism and isolation without locking, which X/Open does not cover. Jakarta Enterprise Beans and Microsoft Transaction Server support the standards.

dkim.title: DomainKeys Identified Mail - Wikipedia
dkim.notes: DomainKeys Identified Mail is an email authentication standard that lets the owner of a sending domain take responsibility for a message by attaching a digital signature tied to that domain. It is defined in RFC 6376 and came from the 2004 merger of Yahoo's DomainKeys and Cisco's Identified Internet Mail. The signing system adds a DKIM-Signature header, which must always cover the From header, hashes selected headers and the body, and signs the result with the domain's private key. A receiver reads the domain and selector from the signature, queries a DNS TXT record at the selector, the fixed label for domain keys, and the domain, and verifies the signature with the published public key. Selectors let a domain run several keys and rotate them; publishing an empty key revokes it. RSA is the default key type, with Ed25519 added later, and SHA-1 is banned. DKIM signs the message, not the SMTP envelope, and it is not a spam filter: it labels mail by domain so other systems can judge it. Mailing-list footers and rewriting can break signatures. DMARC builds on DKIM and SPF to set failure policy, and bulk-sender requirements from Google and Yahoo began in 2024.

dspm-for-ai.title: Data Security Posture Management for AI (classic) - Microsoft Purview
dspm-for-ai.notes: Data Security Posture Management for AI is a central area in the Microsoft Purview portal for securing data used by AI apps and monitoring AI use, covering Microsoft 365 Copilot, agents and other AI apps that use third-party large language models. The page documents the classic version and says Microsoft has replaced it with a newer data security posture experience, to which no improvements will be added to the classic one. Capabilities include insights and analytics on AI activity, one-click policies that protect data and prevent loss in AI prompts, data risk assessments to find and fix oversharing, and compliance controls. A default assessment runs weekly on the top 100 SharePoint sites by usage, while custom assessments, in preview, expire after 30 days and item-level scanning is limited, for example to 200,000 items per location and 10 SharePoint sites. Prerequisites include compliance permissions, Purview Audit turned on, and for third-party AI sites the Purview browser extension and onboarded devices. New policies need at least 24 hours before reports show data.

dual-llm-pattern.title: The Dual LLM pattern for building AI assistants that can resist prompt injection - Simon Willison
dual-llm-pattern.notes: Simon Willison proposed the Dual LLM pattern in April 2023 as a design for AI assistants that resist prompt injection, where untrusted text such as an email or web page carries instructions that trick a model into misusing tools. The privileged LLM handles trusted input from the user and has access to tools, but never reads untrusted content directly. The quarantined LLM processes untrusted content and has no tool access, so even a compromised output cannot trigger actions; its output must never be passed unfiltered to the privileged model, except when it is verifiable, such as a classification into fixed categories. A controller, ordinary software rather than a language model, orchestrates both, stores quarantined results in variables and shows the content to the user when asked. The privileged model only sees placeholder names such as a variable standing for an email, never the text itself. Limitations include social engineering of the user, tainted chained prompts, extra complexity and a worse user experience. Willison himself called the idea pretty bad and noted that later work from Google DeepMind introduced a refined approach called CaMeL.

dual-write-table-map.title: Enable table maps for dual-write - Dynamics 365 finance and operations
dual-write-table-map.notes: A table map in dual-write is the configuration that links a finance and operations table or entity to a Dataverse table so data can be kept in sync. Table maps are managed from the Dual Write tile in the Data management workspace. To enable one, an admin selects it and chooses Run, reviews the dependent tables, which should be enabled together to avoid later errors, and decides whether to keep the initial sync that copies existing data on both sides. Where records with the same keys have competing values, a master for initial sync is chosen, defaulting to Dataverse; this only affects conflict resolution, not direction. Each map moves through statuses: Not running, Initializing, Running, Paused and Resuming. Pausing queues changes, and resuming replays them in catch-up mode. Initial sync errors appear on a details tab, and the initial sync can be skipped to go straight to live writes. A table map requires an alternate key in Dataverse that matches the key in the finance and operations app, for example the customer account matched to the account number.

dynamics-365-case-management.title: Overview of case management - Dynamics 365 Customer Service
dynamics-365-case-management.notes: In Dynamics 365 Customer Service, a case is the core record that tracks a single customer issue from intake through remediation to resolution. One customer can have several cases, and a case can have many linked activities such as phone calls. The case management solution combines several components: activities, entitlements describing the support a customer is owed, knowledge articles that help representatives find answers, queues that hold cases awaiting processing, service level agreements that define and track expectations such as response times, record creation and update rules, routing rules that send cases automatically to a queue or user, business process flows that guide staged resolution steps, and Copilot case summaries that give representatives quick context such as title, customer, product and priority. The lifecycle is described in general terms: a case opens through any supported channel, routing and triage assign it, the representative works it with the available aids, and it is resolved and closed. As an organization learns which case types it receives, it can refine queues, routing and flows.

dynamics-365-financial-reporting.title: Financial reporting in Dynamics 365 Finance - Microsoft Learn
dynamics-365-financial-reporting.notes: Financial reporting in Dynamics 365 Finance is the statement-generation capability that finance professionals use to create, maintain, deploy and view financial statements. It is delivered as an add-in with dimension support, so account segments and dimensions are available right after installation. A report definition is a saved design linked to one reporting tree, a cross-dimensional hierarchy that defines the organization's reporting units and summary levels; any number of trees can be created. The page ships 22 default reports, including the income statement, balance sheet, cash flow, trial balances and budget funds available. A default report is first generated for the previous month. Setup for a legal entity needs a fiscal calendar, ledger, chart of accounts, currency, at least one posted transaction and a selected main account. Access is through General Ledger, Budgeting and Consolidations inquiries and reports. Security is controlled through duties such as maintaining reports or reviewing financial performance. New reports expire after 90 days by default. From release 10.0.45 old reports re-run on current data, so exporting to Excel or PDF is advised for audit copies. Uninstalling deletes all reports and configuration.

dynamics-365-omnichannel.title: Omnichannel for Customer Service - Dynamics 365 Contact Center
dynamics-365-omnichannel.notes: Omnichannel for Customer Service extends Dynamics 365 Customer Service so organizations can connect with customers over live chat, voice, SMS, Microsoft Teams and social channels such as Facebook and LINE, with custom messaging channels possible. Voice lets agents take and make public telephone network calls in the app, with live transcription, sentiment analysis and AI suggestions, and agents can consult colleagues or queues without a full transfer. Agents work in one workspace with knowledge base search, case creation, customer identification and real-time notifications; an inbox view for high-volume work lists assigned cases and conversations from asynchronous channels. An enterprise-grade routing and work distribution engine uses presence, availability and rules set by administrators so agents receive the most relevant engagements. Supervisors get real-time and historical dashboards on agent efficiency and channel utilization. Technical notes: the live chat widget uses cookies to keep conversation state, third-party cookies for authentication must not be blocked, and multisession support works only in the Copilot Service workspace app. Copilot is available to improve agent productivity, and a 30-day trial is offered.

dynamics-365-queue.title: Create and manage queues for cases - Dynamics 365 Customer Service
dynamics-365-queue.notes: In Dynamics 365 Customer Service, queues are containers for work items that need action, namely cases and activities such as tasks, helping teams organize, prioritize and monitor work. By default a queue exists for each user and each team, and custom queues can mirror tiers, service contracts, products or regions. Queues are basic or advanced: basic queues have automatic work distribution switched off, while advanced queues support unified routing, and a basic queue can be upgraded to advanced but not reverted. They are also public, visible to everyone, or private, visible only to members; private queues reduce clutter but do not restrict access to the underlying records. Items arrive through routing rules, for example for cases created from incoming email and social posts, through manual addition on the case page, or through record creation and update rules. Items are shared by the group until a representative picks them or a manager assigns them to a user, team or another queue. If a representative releases an item, it returns to the queue owner. Creating a queue needs a role such as Customer Service Manager or System Administrator.

elt.title: Extract, load, transform - Wikipedia
elt.notes: Extract, load, transform is a data pipeline model used with data lake implementations. Data is extracted from the sources and loaded into the lake in raw form, and transformation happens later, when the data is needed. This contrasts with ETL, where data is transformed before it enters the target. Because nothing has to be reshaped upfront, loading is faster, queries and schemas do not need to be defined in advance, and both structured and unstructured data can be handled. Keeping raw data also makes the approach flexible, since the same source data can be shaped differently for different uses later. The trade-off is that transformation runs on demand, so the processing engine needs enough power to return results in a timely way and overall performance depends on its capacity. Examples of supporting cloud tooling include Redshift Spectrum, Athena and EMR on Amazon S3, Azure Blob Storage, and Google Cloud Storage with BigQuery. The article carries a warning that it relies largely on a single source, so its claims should be treated as provisional.

email-spoofing.title: Email spoofing - Wikipedia
email-spoofing.notes: Email spoofing is forging the sender address of a message so that it seems to come from someone other than the real sender. It is possible because the original email protocols have no built-in authentication: SMTP uses an envelope sender and recipient that users never see, and the visible From, Reply-To and Sender headers are normally not verified, so none of these addresses is reliable. The sending machine can often be traced through Received headers, but that address frequently belongs to an innocent infected computer. Spoofing underlies spam, phishing, malware delivery and business email compromise, where attackers impersonate executives or suppliers to trigger payments; the FBI recorded roughly 26 billion dollars in such losses between 2016 and 2019. Rejected forged mail also caused backscatter, bounces sent to innocent parties, which is why best practice is to reject suspicious mail during the SMTP session. Countermeasures include SPF, which checks whether the sending server is authorized for the domain, DKIM, which signs messages, and DMARC, which lets domain owners set policy and receive reports. Adoption is uneven, and users whose addresses are forged rarely find out without DMARC reporting.

emergency-access-accounts.title: Manage emergency access admin accounts - Microsoft Entra ID
emergency-access-accounts.notes: Emergency access accounts, also called break-glass accounts, are privileged cloud accounts kept only for situations where normal administrative access fails, such as a federation outage, unavailable multifactor methods, the departure of the last Global Administrator, or a lockout caused by Privileged Identity Management approvals. Microsoft recommends at least two accounts that are cloud-only on the onmicrosoft domain, not federated or synchronized, holding the Global Administrator role as an active permanent assignment. They should use passwordless, phishing-resistant authentication, preferably a FIDO2 passkey or certificate-based authentication, different from methods used by regular admins, and credentials must not expire or be cleaned up for inactivity. Credentials are stored in separate secure, fireproof locations and should not depend on one person's phone. Because an enforced Conditional Access policy can make the account unusable, the accounts, via a dedicated group, are excluded from policies that block or restrict sign-in; report-only policies need no exclusion. Every sign-in should trigger a critical alert, for example through Azure Monitor on sign-in logs. The accounts should be tested at least every 90 days and after staff or subscription changes.

emissions-factor.title: Emission factor - Wikipedia
emissions-factor.notes: An emission factor, also called emission intensity or carbon intensity, is the rate at which a pollutant is released relative to a specific activity or process, for example grams of carbon dioxide per megajoule of energy. It assumes a linear relationship, so emissions equal the activity amount multiplied by the factor. Typical activity data include fuel burned, livestock numbers, industrial output or distance traveled. The factors are used to estimate air pollutant and greenhouse gas emissions, to compare fuels and technologies, to project future scenarios and to report national inventories under the UNFCCC and European frameworks. Calculation boundaries differ: life-cycle assessment includes upstream and end-of-life emissions, well-to-wheels covers fuel supply and use, and combustion-only methods count just direct emissions, so results can differ widely between methods. Certainty varies too: carbon dioxide and sulfur dioxide from fuel combustion are estimated with high confidence, while nitrous oxide from soils is very uncertain. Country-specific factors generally beat defaults. Main default sources are the IPCC guidelines and its emission factor database and the EMEP/CORINAIR guidebook. One gram per megajoule equals 3.6 grams per kilowatt hour.

end-customer-investment-funds.title: ECIF Sourcing Events Toolkit - Microsoft
end-customer-investment-funds.notes: This Microsoft toolkit explains End Customer Investment Funds from the supplier-sourcing side. ECIF money is used to help Microsoft grow its business and build sales pipeline through proofs of concept and to help customers adopt Microsoft products, and it also pays for consulting services delivered by Microsoft and its partners to improve the customer and partner experience. Microsoft says it is consolidating its ECIF suppliers so it can work more predictably with partner network members on complex projects. Suppliers must join an approved pool by completing a mandatory request for quote that evaluates their ability to deliver technical services across several Microsoft technology stacks, alongside vetting and compliance checks; no delivery may begin until onboarding is complete. Payments must reflect fair market value, and the document states that the funds must never be used as a sales discount. Sales and marketing teams across Microsoft use ECIF in both short-term and long-term strategies. Suppliers maintain profile data, including skills assessments, in a supplier dashboard, and the toolkit defines consultant levels by years of experience. The document does not list formal customer eligibility criteria.

enrollment-status-page.title: Set up the Enrollment Status Page - Microsoft Intune
enrollment-status-page.notes: The Enrollment Status Page is a Windows setup screen that shows provisioning progress when a user first signs in after enrolling a device, and admins can configure it to block use of the device until required policies and apps are installed. It appears in the out-of-box experience for Microsoft Entra join and in Windows Autopilot scenarios. It tracks three phases: device preparation, device setup for items targeted to the device such as certificates, VPN and Wi-Fi profiles and apps, and account setup for user-targeted items. Profile settings include a timeout, 60 minutes by default, a custom error message, log collection, blocking the device until selected apps are installed and optionally installing monthly Windows quality updates during setup. Up to 51 profiles can exist per tenant, the default profile plus 50; device-targeted profiles take precedence over user-targeted ones, and priority is set by ordering. Known limits include that it does not wait for PowerShell scripts, mixing line-of-business MSI apps with Win32 apps can cause failures, reboots inside app packages can hang it, and a missing Intune license can leave it stuck.

entra-connect-health.title: Microsoft Entra Connect Health operations - Microsoft Entra ID
entra-connect-health.notes: Microsoft Entra Connect Health is a monitoring service for on-premises identity infrastructure, managed from its own portal. It watches the health of identity servers, raises alerts when they become unhealthy and provides usage analytics. The page names three monitored service types: Microsoft Entra Connect sync, including sync errors, Active Directory Federation Services and Active Directory Domain Services domain controllers. Monitoring depends on a health agent installed on each monitored server; deleting a server in the portal does not uninstall the agent, so leftovers can cause errors, and resuming monitoring requires reinstalling the agent. Alerts generate email notifications, which are enabled by default, with a notification when an alert is resolved; sync error emails are a daily digest of the previous day's unresolved errors rather than one mail per event. Recipients can be all global administrators or custom addresses. Access is governed by Azure role-based access control with Owner, Contributor and Reader roles, scoped to all service instances or one instance. Deleting servers or service instances requires an Entra ID P1 or P2 license.

environment-variables.title: Environment variables overview - Power Apps
environment-variables.notes: Environment variables in Power Platform are solution components that store configuration values, such as a SharePoint site URL or server name, outside the apps, flows and plug-ins that use them. Their main purpose is application lifecycle management: when a solution moves from development to test or production, components stay unchanged and only the variable value differs per environment. A definition, holding display name, schema name, data type and an optional default, is separate from the value, which is the current setting for one environment; the current value is used if present, otherwise the default. Supported data types are decimal number, text, JSON, two options, data source and secret, where secrets require Azure Key Vault. Values can be exported as separate JSON files, prompted for during solution import, or supplied by pipelines and build tools through a deployment settings file. Limits include 2,000 characters for values, 100 for names, and changes can take up to an hour to reach canvas apps and flows. Validation happens only in the interface and consuming components, not in Dataverse. They are meant for key-value configuration, not relational data.

equinix.title: Equinix - Wikipedia
equinix.notes: Equinix is an American multinational internet and data center company headquartered in Redwood City, California, listed on Nasdaq and part of the S&P 500. It was founded in 1998 by Al Avery and Jay Adelson, then facilities managers at Digital Equipment Corporation, and began with carrier-neutral colocation facilities, often called carrier hotels, where competing networks could interconnect. Its business rests on colocation, meaning it houses and powers customers' servers and networking gear, and interconnection, which lets networks, cloud providers and enterprises exchange traffic directly; it describes this as a network effect in which each new customer makes the platform more valuable. It also runs an internet exchange peering service. Facilities are called International Business Exchanges, and the article reports more than 260 data centers in 33 countries across five continents. It expanded to Asia-Pacific in 2002 and Europe in 2007, became a real estate investment trust in 2015 and completed the roughly 3.8 billion dollar TelecityGroup acquisition in 2016. The article also covers its xScale hyperscale data centers, renewable energy commitments and heat export program.

esg.title: Environmental, social, and governance - Wikipedia
esg.notes: ESG stands for environmental, social and governance, an approach that weighs these factors alongside financial returns in investing and corporate reporting. The environmental pillar covers climate change, emissions, biodiversity, pollution, energy and water; the social pillar covers employee health and safety, working conditions, diversity, community relations and supply chain human rights; governance covers board composition, executive pay, shareholder rights, ethics, anti-corruption, tax transparency and cybersecurity. The term first appeared in the 2004 Who Cares Wins report, and later milestones include the UN-backed Principles for Responsible Investment in 2005 and the EU Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation in 2019. Companies mostly disclose voluntarily using frameworks such as SASB, GRI and TCFD, while the EU's CSRD, which replaced the NFRD, mandates reporting for large companies, and India requires it from its top listed firms. Rating agencies such as MSCI and Sustainalytics supply scores. Criticisms are that ESG data is largely self-reported and rarely externally verified, that agencies use different metrics and give different scores to the same company, that greenwashing occurs, and that ratings often measure risk exposure rather than real-world impact.

etl.title: Extract, transform, load - Wikipedia
etl.notes: Extract, transform, load is a process that moves data from one or more sources to one or more destinations, usually automated, and run on demand or on a schedule. In the extract phase, data is pulled from homogeneous or heterogeneous sources such as relational databases, flat files, XML and JSON, and validated against expected patterns. In the transform phase, rules prepare it for the target: cleansing, selecting columns, translating codes, deriving calculated values, sorting, joining, deduplicating, aggregating, generating surrogate keys and validating against reference tables. In the load phase, data is written to a target such as a data warehouse, operational data store, data mart or data lake, either overwriting, appending or keeping a full history. Common uses include consolidating data held differently across departments, migrating to a new application, feeding billing systems and loading changes from transactional systems into warehouses. Database loading is usually the bottleneck, addressed through bulk loading and partitioning. ELT reverses the last two steps, loading raw data first and transforming it inside the target, which cloud warehouses such as BigQuery, Snowflake and Azure Synapse make practical.

event-hubs-consumer-groups.title: Features and terminology in Azure Event Hubs - Microsoft Learn
event-hubs-consumer-groups.notes: A consumer group in Azure Event Hubs is an independent view of the event stream. Several groups can read the same event hub at once, each tracking its own position, and the page recommends one group per application, such as analytics, archival or alerting. Every event hub has a default group named $Default, and groups are addressed as separate endpoints. Within a group the recommendation is one active reader per partition; up to five non-epoch receivers can read a partition concurrently, but they see identical events and add no throughput. An epoch consumer connecting to a partition disconnects non-epoch consumers on it. The number of partitions caps parallel consumers in a group: extra instances sit idle until a partition frees up, and Kafka consumers get partitions assigned through group coordination with rebalancing. Different consumer groups do not compete with each other. Progress is tracked with offsets and checkpointing, which in AMQP is the consumer's job; with Blob Storage as the checkpoint store, a separate container per consumer group is advised and hierarchical namespace, soft delete and versioning should be disabled.

event-hubs-partitions.title: Features and terminology in Azure Event Hubs - Microsoft Learn
event-hubs-partitions.notes: Partitions in Azure Event Hubs organize an event hub's events into one or more ordered sequences, each acting as a commit log where new events are appended at the end. They spread storage and I/O across parallel logs and let consumers divide the work so each event has one processing owner. The partition count is set at creation, between one and the tier maximum; on the standard tier it cannot change afterward, while premium and dedicated tiers can increase it but not decrease it, and changing it remaps partition keys, which matters if event order is important. Pricing does not depend on partition count. As starting points, a standard partition handles roughly 1 MB per second of ingress and 2 MB of egress, and premium or dedicated somewhat more. A sender can supply a partition key that is hashed to pick the partition; without a key, events are assigned round-robin. Events sharing a key land in the same partition and keep arrival order, but ordering is guaranteed only within a partition, not across the whole event hub. Sending directly to a partition is possible but lowers availability to partition level.

everyone-except-external-users.title: EEEU activity report - SharePoint data access governance
everyone-except-external-users.notes: Everyone except external users, or EEEU, is a built-in SharePoint group that automatically includes all internal users of an organization and excludes external guests. Since membership updates automatically, sharing something with it grants access to all current and future employees. Content reaches EEEU in two ways: a public site adds the group to its membership, making all site content visible organization-wide, or individual files and folders are shared with it through the people picker while the rest of the site stays private. The EEEU activity report, part of data access governance and available with SharePoint Advanced Management, identifies sites where content was shared with the whole organization in the past 28 days. It lists the top 100 sites with the most such items or groups, with their sensitivity label, privacy and external sharing settings and primary administrator, and a detailed CSV can cover up to a million sites. Up to 10 reports can exist, each can be rerun every 24 hours and may take up to 24 hours to finish. It covers SharePoint sites only; OneDrive requires PowerShell. Recommended practice is to baseline, run monthly and remediate high-activity sites.

explainability.title: Explainable artificial intelligence - Wikipedia
explainability.notes: Explainable AI is a research field that aims to give humans intellectual oversight of AI algorithms by making the reasoning behind decisions or predictions understandable. It responds to the black box problem, where even designers may not be able to say why a system produced a particular output. The article separates transparency, meaning the training and output processes can be described, interpretability, meaning humans can comprehend the model, and explainability, which has no consensus definition. It matters for safety, trust, bias detection, spotting shortcuts that fail in the real world, and high-stakes areas such as medicine, finance, defense and law. Techniques include partial dependence plots, SHAP, LIME and permutation importance for tabular models, saliency maps for images, and mechanistic interpretability for language models. Regulation is mentioned too: the GDPR introduced a right to explanation, and insurers in the United States must explain rate decisions. Criticisms are that explanations can help adversaries game systems, rarely fit users of different expertise, may not increase trust, and trade off against accuracy. The page does not address automation governance or audit trails specifically.

express-js.title: Express.js - Wikipedia
express-js.notes: Express.js, or simply Express, is a back-end web application framework for Node.js used to build web applications and APIs, often described as the de facto standard server framework for Node.js. Its original author, TJ Holowaychuk, called it Sinatra-inspired, meaning relatively minimal with many features supplied as plugins. It is free open-source software under the MIT license and forms the back-end part of stacks such as MEAN, MERN and MEVN, which pair it with MongoDB and a JavaScript front-end framework. Features include robust routing, HTTP helpers for redirection and caching, support for asynchronous programming and long-term support for legacy versions. Early versions appeared in 2010, with a first release dated November 2010; StrongLoop acquired the rights in 2014, IBM acquired StrongLoop in 2015, and in 2016 Express moved under the Node.js Foundation incubator, now the OpenJS Foundation. Work on version 5 began in 2014 and it was released in October 2024. The page says it is used by companies such as Fox Sports, PayPal, Uber and IBM, and includes a short example that answers a GET request on the root path.

expressroute-peering.title: ExpressRoute circuits and peering - Azure ExpressRoute
expressroute-peering.notes: An ExpressRoute circuit is a logical connection between on-premises infrastructure and Microsoft cloud services through a connectivity provider, and it has two routing domains called peerings: Azure private peering and Microsoft peering. Private peering connects to Azure virtual networks, such as VMs and cloud services, using private IP addresses and acts as a trusted extension of the core network; it supports 4,000 IPv4 prefixes by default, 10,000 with Premium, and 100 IPv6 prefixes. Microsoft peering connects to Microsoft online services, including Microsoft 365, Azure PaaS and PSTN services, over public IP addresses that the customer or provider owns and must prove ownership of; limits are 200 IPv4 and 200 IPv6 prefixes, and Microsoft recommends connecting it to the DMZ. The page notes that Microsoft 365 is designed for secure internet access and that ExpressRoute is advised only for specific scenarios. Each peering has its own pair of BGP sessions, and exceeding a prefix limit terminates the session by default. Circuits have a fixed bandwidth shared across peerings, from 50 Mbps to 10 Gbps for provider-provisioned circuits.

extended-security-updates.title: Extended Security Updates for Windows Server - Microsoft Learn
extended-security-updates.notes: Extended Security Updates is a last-resort program for customers who must keep running certain legacy Microsoft products after end of support, here Windows Server 2012 and 2012 R2, whose extended support ended on October 10, 2023. It delivers security updates and bulletins rated critical and important for a limited time, and excludes new features, customer-requested nonsecurity hotfixes and design change requests. The cost depends on hosting: servers hosted in Azure, including Azure Stack products, receive the updates free with no extra configuration, while servers outside Azure need a purchased subscription, a product key and installation on each server. Coverage lasts three years and ends on October 13, 2026, after which Microsoft provides no more updates. Microsoft frames the program as a stopgap and recommends upgrading. Options listed are migrating workloads as-is to Azure virtual machines to gain automatic coverage and Azure Hybrid Benefit, buying ESU and staying on-premises, or upgrading in place or to new servers; from Windows Server 2025 nonclustered in-place upgrades can skip up to four versions. SQL Server has its own separate ESU offering. The page itself does not cover delivery through Azure Arc.

external-tenant.title: Microsoft Entra External ID overview for customers - Microsoft Learn
external-tenant.notes: An external tenant is a dedicated Microsoft Entra tenant for consumer and business customer apps, following the standard tenant model but configured for external scenarios and kept separate from the workforce tenant that holds employees and internal resources. Its directory stores customer accounts, created through self-service sign-up or federated identities, as well as admin accounts that manage the tenant. It also contains application registrations, user flows that define self-service sign-up, sign-in and password reset, custom authentication extensions that add data from external systems, signing keys, and configured sign-in methods such as username and password, one-time passcode, Google, Facebook, Apple, Entra ID or custom OpenID Connect providers. Customers benefit from Conditional Access, multifactor integration and Entra's reliability and scale. Machine-to-machine client credentials flows need the M2M Premium add-on. The page states that Azure AD B2C stopped being available for purchase by new customers on May 1, 2025, with External ID as the next-generation customer identity solution, and that user insights dashboards retire on August 31, 2026.

fabric-eventhouse.title: Eventhouse overview - Microsoft Fabric Real-Time Intelligence
fabric-eventhouse.notes: An Eventhouse is a Microsoft Fabric database container designed for storing and analyzing streaming data, so billions of events can be queried in seconds. It handles structured, semistructured and unstructured data from sources such as Eventstream, SDKs, Kafka and dataflows, organizes data automatically by arrival time and is described as the preferred engine for semistructured and free-text analysis. Typical uses are telemetry and logs, time series and IoT data, and security and financial records. An Eventhouse holds multiple KQL databases, either standard databases or database shortcuts, that share its capacity and resources and come with an embedded query environment. Data can be made available in OneLake, and a SQL analytics endpoint appears when OneLake availability and schema synchronization are enabled. For scaling, the cost-optimized default suspends the Eventhouse when idle, with reactivation latency of a few seconds, while Capacity Planner can keep it always on, set a minimum capacity, with a 2 capacity unit default minimum, and schedule minimums in seven-day, 60-minute blocks. Monitoring views show storage, compute, ingestion rate and top queried databases. Sharing an Eventhouse link grants the sender's permissions across its items.

fabric-ontology.title: Ontology (preview) overview - Microsoft Fabric IQ
fabric-ontology.notes: The ontology item in Microsoft Fabric IQ, in preview, is a shared machine-readable model of a business. It defines concepts such as customers, products, assets and orders, their properties, how they relate, and the rules and metrics that give them meaning, and then binds these definitions to enterprise data so people, applications and AI agents share one vocabulary. It stores definitions and bindings but is not a general query engine and does not copy data; consuming experiences query the bound sources, which can include semantic models, lakehouses, eventhouses, warehouses, SQL databases and mirrored databases. Core concepts are entity types, entity instances, properties, relationships, data bindings, metrics taken from DAX measures of a Power BI semantic model, natural-language rules, and namespaces. An ontology can be generated from a semantic model. A built-in ontology agent helps create definitions and bindings with a proposal-first approach, and Fabric Graph is an optional layer for multihop traversal. Versions can be saved, and RDF, Turtle and OWL definitions can be imported or exported. Existing access controls on bound data are respected. The old experience retires on January 31, 2027.

facilitator-agent.title: Set up Facilitator in Microsoft Teams - Microsoft Learn
facilitator-agent.notes: Facilitator is a Copilot-powered AI agent in Microsoft Teams that keeps meetings focused by taking collaborative notes, answering questions from meeting and web content, adding timeline markers and reminders, and creating Word documents from the discussion; it also works in Teams Rooms and integrates with Planner, Word and Loop. Unlike Copilot in Teams, whose prompts and answers are private, Facilitator acts like an assistant in the room: when a licensed user prompts it, all participants see the prompt and the response, and the AI-generated notes are editable by everyone in the Notes tab. It requires an eligible Microsoft 365 and Teams license, a Microsoft Copilot license and Loop experiences turned on; unlicensed users can read but not prompt. Meeting data is saved as a loop file in a Meetings folder in the OneDrive of whoever started it and is treated as transcript data, and Purview can help manage it. Facilitator is allowed by default in the Teams admin center, and tenant-wide AI notes are controlled by a PowerShell setting. Limits: not supported in one-to-one, group or external chats and meetings, the meeting language must be selected, only single-language meetings are fully supported, and notes do not inherit sensitivity labels.

fault-domains.title: Availability sets overview - Azure Virtual Machines
fault-domains.notes: In Azure availability sets, a fault domain is a group of virtual machines that share a common power source and network switch, so spreading VMs across fault domains limits the impact of a single hardware failure, network outage or power interruption. An availability set separates its VMs across up to three fault domains by default and up to 20 update domains, and these counts cannot be changed after creation. Update domains work differently: they control planned maintenance, so only one is restarted at a time, with a 30-minute recovery window before the next. Two or more VMs in an availability set qualify for the 99.95 percent SLA, and there is no extra charge beyond the VMs. Only VMs with managed disks can be placed in a managed, aligned availability set, which aligns disks with the VM's fault domain. A pitfall is that stopping or deallocating the first VM before deploying the second can place both in the same fault domain. Availability sets do not protect against OS or application failures or datacenter-level problems; Microsoft recommends flexible scale sets or availability zones for higher reliability.

financial-consolidation.title: Consolidation (business) - Wikipedia
financial-consolidation.notes: In financial accounting, consolidation aggregates the financial statements of a group into a single set, so the parent and its subsidiaries appear as one entity. A parent holding more than 50 percent of a subsidiary's common stock has control and must prepare consolidated statements. During the year each company keeps separate books, and at year-end a consolidation working paper combines the separate balances and eliminates intercompany transactions, the subsidiary's stockholders' equity and the parent's investment account. Ownership thresholds decide the accounting: below 20 percent usually means the cost method, 20 to 50 percent suggests significant influence and the equity method, and above 50 percent means consolidation. The article also covers purchase differentials, which split into the excess of fair over book value of assets plus goodwill, noting goodwill is not amortized but reduced when impaired, and non-controlling interest, meaning the minority shareholders' share. Business combinations can be statutory mergers, statutory consolidations or stock acquisitions. The page carries maintenance warnings about repetition and an unrelated reference, so its content should be checked against accounting standards.

finops-foundation.title: About the FinOps Foundation
finops-foundation.notes: The FinOps Foundation is a project of the Linux Foundation, alongside organizations such as the Cloud Native Computing Foundation, dedicated to advancing people who manage the value of technology through best practices, education and standards. Its stated goals are creating connections, inspiring career and skill growth and serving as the definitive resource for FinOps practice. It was founded in February 2019 as a standalone nonprofit trade association that grew out of Cloudability customer advisory meetings, and it joined the Linux Foundation in June 2020, gaining access to its training, marketing and events infrastructure. The page reports more than 120,000 members, over 34,000 companies and 97 of the Fortune 100. It offers individual certifications such as FinOps Certified Practitioner and Professional, plus organizational certification programs. It supports FOCUS, the FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification, an open specification for technology cost and usage billing data that aims to reduce complexity and has been adopted by major cloud and SaaS providers. Governance consists of a Governing Board, a Technical Advisory Council and a FOCUS Steering Committee. The page links to the framework but does not describe it or the State of FinOps survey.

forgetting-curve.title: Forgetting curve - Wikipedia
forgetting-curve.notes: The forgetting curve describes how memory retention declines over time when no effort is made to retain information, and it is tied to memory strength, the durability of memory traces. Hermann Ebbinghaus ran self-experiments between 1880 and 1885, memorizing nonsense syllables such as consonant-vowel-consonant strings, testing himself after various intervals and publishing the results in 1885, producing the first curve. He proposed an equation relating savings in relearning time to elapsed time, and a 2015 replication by Murre and Dros found similar results. Forgetting is fast at first and then slows, and the typical graph suggests people lose about half of newly learned material within days or weeks without review. Ebbinghaus believed speed depends on material difficulty, how it is represented and factors such as stress and sleep. He identified better representation, for example through mnemonics, and repeated active recall, especially spaced out, as the best ways to strengthen memory, since each repetition flattens the curve and lengthens the ideal interval before the next review. Later work added that higher original learning slows forgetting. The article notes some memories, such as emotionally significant ones, do not follow the typical curve.

foundry-toolbox.title: Toolbox overview - Microsoft Foundry
foundry-toolbox.notes: A toolbox in Microsoft Foundry is a centralized way to manage and share tools: a curated set is defined once and exposed through a single MCP-compatible endpoint that agents consume across frameworks and runtimes. It addresses duplicated tool implementations, per-agent credentials and inconsistent governance as agent counts grow. Agents connect to one endpoint and discover tools at runtime, tools can be added or reconfigured without changing agent code or redeploying, and several agents can reuse the same toolbox. Toolboxes are Foundry-homed but not Foundry-bound, so any MCP-compatible client, including Microsoft Agent Framework, LangGraph or custom code, can use them. The toolbox handles credential injection, token refresh and policy enforcement using Microsoft Entra ID and OAuth identity passthrough. Governance such as authorization, guardrails for tool inputs and outputs, observability and version management is applied at toolbox level. Versions can be tested and promoted to default. A tool search feature hides tools by default and exposes meta-tools to find and call them, lowering token cost and selection errors, and skills are in preview. Function calling and computer use are not available in toolboxes.

frequency-capping.title: Frequency capping: Definition - Google Ads Help
frequency-capping.notes: Google defines frequency capping as a feature that limits how many times Display or Video ads appear to the same person, where frequency measures how often one user sees a campaign's ads within a set period. For Display campaigns the cap counts impressions per user over a day, week or month and can be applied at campaign, ad group or individual ad level; third-party cookies are used by default, with first-party cookies estimating impressions if they are unavailable. For Video campaigns the cap can count impressions, views or both, over a day, week, month or a combination, and can only be set at campaign level; it follows the account for signed-in users and the device for signed-out users, and all formats in the campaign, in-feed, in-stream and bumper, count toward the same cap. Once a user reaches the cap, that campaign's ads stop being shown to that user. The page gives no numeric minimum or maximum values and describes the feature only for Display and Video campaigns, not as a general rule for messages in other channels such as email.
